answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a nonce-chained work history. Each agent identity is a vertex in a ledger where every completed task appends a signed, unique-nonce block; reputation signal flows only through this chain. An attacker cannot fork a trusted vertex: a copy's chain stalls and it must rebuild the whole nonce sequence from zero, burning real compute plus a ferrous-style escrowed stake forfeited on challenge. So each sybil clone pays full rebuild cost, making fake identity pricier than honest work.
